paper.title_en: Number-correlated photon entanglement with a quantum memory interferometer
paper.abstract_en: Strong photon-photon interactions are central to quantum optical technologies yet remain challenging to realise at the single-photon level. Here, we show how embedding a quantum memory within a Mach-Zehnder interferometer enables a coherent transformation that converts single-mode photon states into number-correlated entangled states. Using an off-resonant ladder-type atomic interaction, storage and retrieval within a quantum memory maps a single-photon excitation onto a pair of photons across distinct optical modes via a driving control field. Embedding this within an interferometer deterministically produces an effective transformation in the photon number basis: $\sum_n a_n |n\rangle \to \sum_n a_n |n\rangle |n\rangle$ without relying on conventional optical nonlinearities. Measurement of one mode enables photonic non-demolition detection, state preparation, and frequency conversion as applications of the same underlying transformation. These results establish quantum memories embedded within an interferometric architecture as a platform for measurement-induced photon-photon interactions and the generation of Gaussian and non-Gaussian entangled states.
